_comment: Per-row disposition for every preflight advisory pinned in example_fidelity_snapshot.json (#737 item 1). The snapshot pins WHAT each audited example emits; this file says WHY each of those rows is there, so the gate is a zero-UNEXPLAINED-advisory bar rather than a drift pin. Entries are keyed by (variant, code) and carry the number of pinned rows that pair covers -- rows that share a code on one variant are the same condition on different ports, axes or entities, and the snapshot already pins each one's full text. test_example_fidelity_contract.py asserts the mapping is a bijection and that the row counts add up, so a new advisory, a removed one, or a stale entry all fail. disposition: 'intended' = the example deliberately shows or tolerates this condition (reason cites the example's own docstring/comment or the physics); 'defect-open' = the example should not emit this and the fix needs work beyond this file's PR, with the issue number that tracks it. A defect small enough to fix leaves no entry -- the row is gone from the snapshot instead. validation/crossval/* scripts are frozen research records (#928): their rows are classified here, never edited. anchor holds, for each line chunk of ref, the stripped text of its first and last lines, and the contract asserts the file still has that text there, so a ref moved by an edit above it fails.

(Two earlier probe-clearance rows named this tutorial's own finite ground sheet as the reflector, at -11.25 mm; a conductor at the port's ground reference is no longer a reflector candidate, so they are gone.)

The tutorial keeps its geometry and mesh under #1512, like the two validation notch builders: its through-line leaves realized tails of 3.1625 mm (declared 3.25 mm) behind both ports. With eps_eff=2.405090 and an open-end extension of 0.3645 mm the effective length is 3.527 mm and its quarter-wave frequency 13.7022 GHz, outside the refusal interval for the 0..6 GHz read. Both findings are advisory; the geometry is deliberately unchanged.

entries.reason: The scene is the one-cell parallel-plate TEM channel of the lumped/wire port battery: PEC plates on z, PMC side walls on y one cell apart, so the lumped port's Ez edge necessarily lies on the y_lo magnetic-wall plane. The advisory itself states that the Yee magnetic image keeps tangential E on that face coupled to the interior and that a lumped port there describes the full symmetric object; the check's G1 gate confirms the port couples (mean |S11|^2 = 0.25).

This example declares its copper with add_thin_conductor at the API's default 35 um, solved with zero thickness, on a 1.5 mm substrate (t/h 2.33 %). The advisory states that the declared thickness is not in the model and that a strip or patch on this substrate reads electrically long by about 0.27 % (#1523 table); that is true of this example and is the known limitation 'Conductor thickness is not solved' in docs/guides/known_limitations.md. The ground sheet (thin_conductors[0]) covers the substrate footprint and is not reported; only the patch (thin_conductors[1]) is.
